brief: Goldman's Rich Privorotsky argues the AI model layer has no moat. A week in which Google reportedly tested a new model (Carbon) flipped Polymarket's best-model-by-2026-year-end odds to Google 43%, Anthropic 42%, OpenAI 9%, Meta 3%, xAI 2%, reversing Anthropic's prior lead. Because model leadership resets quarterly, he says the durable edge sits with whoever owns powered, operational compute, which stays scarce because the street cannot bring power and data-center capacity online fast enough: about half of 2026-slated US data centers are delayed or canceled, Wood Mackenzie found over two-thirds of sought US data-center power will not materialize, and Goldman's commodity team expects behind-the-meter generation to supply 25% of data centers by 2030, up from near zero in 2025. That scarcity lets hyperscalers command premium pricing, contingent on token demand outpacing falling token prices. An FT report that OpenAI's annualized revenue run-rate is near $50bn, $20bn below a previously circulated figure, triggered a hedge-fund rotation out of Info Tech, the week's most-sold sector after four of the prior five weeks as most-bought. Privorotsky attributes the gap to gross-versus-net revenue accounting, not demand, but flags the reaction as a crowding signal. ASML and TSMC report this week as the next test.
